paragraphs.title: Gathering the Nations and Judging Them for Their Harm to Israel

easy.explanation: The LORD says that He will bring the nations down into the valley of Jehoshaphat.
easy.q: To what place will the LORD gather the nations?

easy.explanation: The nations scattered Israel, parted the LORD's land, and sold His people.
easy.q: For what will the LORD plead with or judge the nations?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that they 'parted my land.'
easy.q: What did the nations do to the LORD's land?

answers: The nations will be gathered for judgment
The nations will return home peacefully
medium.explanation: After restoring Judah and Jerusalem, the LORD will gather the nations and plead with them.
medium.q: What will happen after the LORD brings again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: As recompence for selling the children of Judah
So they can work the land
So they can learn the law
medium.explanation: The judgment reverses the nations' treatment of Judah's children.
medium.q: Why will the children of the nations be sold into the hand of the children of Judah?

answers: The nations divided the LORD's land among themselves
medium.explanation: The nations are accused of dividing the LORD's land.
medium.q: What does the phrase 'parted my land' mean in context?

answers: The wrongdoers receive a reversal of what they did
The victims must leave the land
challenge.explanation: Those who sold Judah's children will see their own children handed over to Judah.
challenge.q: What principle of recompence is shown in this passage?

answers: Restoration of Judah, gathering of the nations, and judgment
Judgment of the nations, restoration of Judah, and gathering
Division of the land, peace with the nations, and exile
challenge.explanation: The LORD first restores Judah and Jerusalem, then gathers and judges the nations.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly follows the events in these verses?

answers: The nations took valuable treasures and carried them into their temples
The nations used the treasures to water the land
challenge.explanation: The nations had taken the LORD's silver and gold and carried His pleasant things into their temples.
challenge.q: What do the silver, gold, and pleasant things taken into the temples show?

easy.explanation: They are told to proclaim war and prepare for battle.
easy.q: What are the nations called to prepare for?

easy.explanation: Plowshares will become swords and pruninghooks will become spears.
easy.q: What will be beaten into swords and spears?

easy.explanation: The command says, 'let all the men of war draw near.'
easy.q: Who is called to come to war?

answers: So that everyone will join the gathering for war
So that they can learn farming
So that they will flee from the battle
medium.explanation: The command presents a complete mobilization, including those considered weak.
medium.q: Why are the weak told to say, 'I am strong'?

answers: To be judged by the LORD
medium.explanation: The LORD says that He will sit there to judge all the heathen round about.
medium.q: What is the purpose of gathering in the valley of Jehoshaphat?

medium.explanation: Pruninghooks were farming tools that the nations are told to turn into spears.

answers: It shows the change from ordinary farming to preparation for war
It announces the end of warfare
It represents a return to peaceful farming
challenge.explanation: Tools of cultivation are transformed into weapons of battle.
challenge.q: What is the significance of turning agricultural tools into weapons?

answers: It summons them to assemble from every direction
It sends them away from Judah
challenge.explanation: The nations are commanded to assemble and gather themselves together round about.
challenge.q: How does the call to the nations move them toward the valley of Jehoshaphat?

answers: Their gathering for war brings them to the place where the LORD will judge them
Judgment takes place before they are summoned
challenge.explanation: They are gathered in the valley of Jehoshaphat, where the LORD will sit to judge them.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the nations' preparation for war and their judgment?

paragraphs.title: The Day of the Lord and Final Judgment

easy.explanation: The passage uses the sickle, harvest, press, and overflowing fats as judgment images.
easy.q: What images are used to describe the judgment?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, 'The sun and the moon shall be darkened.'
easy.q: What will happen to the sun and moon on the day of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD will be the hope of His people and the strength of the children of Israel.
easy.q: Who will be the hope and strength of Israel?

answers: Because the wickedness of the nations is great
Because the land is flourishing peacefully
Because the war has ended without judgment
medium.explanation: The ripe harvest and full winepress picture the time when the nations' wickedness has reached its fullness.
medium.q: Why is the harvest described as ripe and the winepress as full?

answers: The heavens and the earth shake
medium.explanation: The passage says that the heavens and the earth shall shake.
medium.q: What happens when the LORD roars out of Zion and utters His voice from Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The sickle is a harvesting tool used here as a symbol of judgment.

answers: The world shakes, but the LORD protects Israel
Israel shakes, but the nations are protected
Everything is peaceful and there is no judgment
challenge.explanation: The heavens and earth shake, yet the LORD remains the hope and strength of His people.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast on the day of the LORD?

answers: The judgment is portrayed in both agricultural and cosmic terms
challenge.explanation: Judgment is first pictured as harvest and pressing grapes, then as an event affecting the heavens and earth.
challenge.q: What does the movement from harvest imagery to darkness and shaking show?

answers: Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will no longer pass through her
Jerusalem will be given to the nations
challenge.explanation: The LORD says that Jerusalem shall be holy and that no strangers shall pass through her any more.
challenge.q: What will be the result for Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that the mountains shall drop down new wine.
easy.q: What will drop down from the mountains?

easy.explanation: The rivers of Judah shall flow with waters.
easy.q: What will flow through all the rivers of Judah?

answers: From the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: The fountain shall come forth from the house of the LORD.
easy.q: From where will the fountain come?

answers: As a land flowing with new wine, milk, and water
As a dry and empty land
As a land filled with continual war
medium.explanation: The mountains, hills, rivers, and fountain all present an image of abundance.
medium.q: How is Judah described in that day?

medium.explanation: The fountain shall water the valley of Shittim.
medium.q: What will the fountain from the house of the LORD water?

medium.explanation: New wine is fresh produce from the grape harvest, symbolizing abundance.
medium.q: What does 'new wine' refer to in this verse?

answers: The preparation of the nations for war
challenge.explanation: The flowing wine, milk, and water create a picture of life and prosperity.
challenge.q: What central idea is expressed by the flowing waters and new wine?

challenge.explanation: The verse specifically emphasizes that a fountain comes from the house of the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the special source of the abundance described in the verse?

answers: They all contribute to a picture of a fruitful and watered land
They are all described as ruined places
They all serve as hiding places for the nations
challenge.explanation: The mountains provide new wine, the hills milk, the rivers water, and the fountain further waters the land.
challenge.q: How do the mountains, hills, rivers, and fountain function together in the description?

paragraphs.title: Desolation of the Nations, Judah's Permanence, and Retribution for Bloodshed

easy.explanation: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness.
easy.q: What will happen to Egypt and Edom?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, 'Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.'
The final words declare that the LORD dwelleth in Zion.
easy.q: Where will the LORD dwell at the end of the passage?

answers: Because of violence against Judah and innocent bloodshed
medium.explanation: Their desolation is punishment for violence against Judah and for shedding innocent blood.
medium.q: Why will Egypt and Edom become desolate?

answers: The nations become desolate, while Judah and Jerusalem endure
All of them remain in the same condition
Judah becomes desolate while the nations prosper
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts the desolation of Egypt and Edom with the permanence of Judah and Jerusalem.
medium.q: What contrast is made between Egypt and Edom and Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: The blood of people who were not guilty
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to people who were killed despite having no guilt deserving death.
medium.q: What does the phrase 'innocent blood' mean?

answers: The blood will not remain without judgment or recompence
The blood will cleanse the nations
challenge.explanation: The LORD declares that He will address the bloodshed that had previously gone unpunished.
challenge.q: What is meant by the statement, 'I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed'?

answers: The violent nations are punished, while Judah and Jerusalem endure
The violent nations inherit Judah, while Jerusalem disappears
The actions of the nations have no consequence
challenge.explanation: Punishment for bloodshed is set against the continuing existence of Judah and Jerusalem.
challenge.q: How does the ending strengthen the theme of justice?

answers: Desolation of the nations, permanence of Judah, judgment for bloodshed, and the LORD dwelling in Zion
Abundance in Judah, sale of captives, and the LORD leaving Zion
Preparation for war, division of the land, and abandonment of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The conclusion moves from the nations' punishment to Judah's permanence, blood-guilt judgment, and the LORD's dwelling in Zion.
challenge.q: What is the sequence of ideas in the final verses?
